task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fractious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fractious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By day three in the jury room, the twelve had grown fractious, quarreling over lunch orders as sharply as over the timeline.
Cranky is a mood one nap can fix; fractious has turned outward — snapping, digging in, making trouble for whoever's in charge.
Uncontrollable goes past fractious: nothing the handler tries works at all anymore.

Unruly means hard to control — a crowd that won't form lines, hair that won't lie flat — and it needs no bad temper at all. Fractious adds the irritability: a fractious group is hard to manage because it is snappish and quarrelsome, scraping against its handlers and itself. Unruly disobeys; fractious disobeys crossly.

Peevish is whiny and easily annoyed, usually one person at a time, sulking over small discomforts. Fractious scales up and turns outward: a fractious jury or touring quartet quarrels, digs in, and makes real trouble for whoever has to manage it. Peevish grumbles in its corner; fractious fights the whole room.

A fraction is literally a piece broken off the whole — one part of something divided.
Fractious means troublesome or irritable.
Three weeks into the tour, the quartet has gone fractious.

The first violin and the violist are quarreling about bowings, the bowing quarrel is secretly about the thermostat in the van, and this morning the second violin threatened to quit over a parking space.
Their manager has begun scheduling rest days the way paramedics schedule shifts.
Fractious is the exact word because it names the state of being troublesome and irritable — friction-prone, snappish, hard to manage.
It isn't hatred and it isn't a feud; nobody in the van is an enemy.
The group is simply worn to the point where everything scrapes, and every small thing breaks into quarrel.
Fractious is for the irritable and hard-to-manage — overtired children, balky animals, committees at hour three.

Its cluster-mates in this unit argue on purpose: a contentious person disputes claims and a pugnacious one wants the fight, but a fractious group has no agenda at all beyond being impossible to steer.
If one adult is merely grumbling, cranky is the humbler, truer word.

The film called for twelve trained goats, and the wrangler warned the director on day one.
Goats, she said, are not sheep; a herd of them is fractious on its best morning.
By the second week the animals were butting the boom operator, nipping one another over shade, and refusing, as one, to cross their marks.
It was not simple disorder -- there was temper in it, aimed at handlers and herd-mates alike.
The wrangler finally shot the scene at dawn, one goat at a time, because managing them together had defeated three professionals and a drone.
